body.statement: For every \(I\in\mathfrak J_2^{\mathrm{nw}}\), if every nontrivial variable in \(V\) is binary and \(g\) uses \(\ell\ge1\) original response blocks, then exact sharp endpoints and rational attaining finite SCMs are computable without a width assumption in \(B^{O(\ell(1+\log B)^2)}\) bit operations. The algorithm enumerates supports only through the exact raw rank of each relevant block and obtains one rational feasible point for every irrelevant block.
body.justification: This gives a second exact regime when a useful decomposition is unavailable but the query touches few original roots.
body.gap: Arroyo et al. obtain polynomial-cardinality column generation for one intervention; the proposed logarithmic-square rank bound covers several explicitly represented relevant blocks and an objective of degree at least three.
body.consumer: A canonical optimizer can dispatch sparse-block binary queries even when its measured scalar response width is large.
